evals.prompt: Split the terminal and open a second pane on the right with zsh.
evals.expected_output: Agent uses cmux new-pane --type terminal to create a new terminal pane, not new-split from Claude Code context.

assertions.name: uses-new-pane-not-new-split
assertions.description: Response uses 'cmux new-pane --type terminal' rather than 'cmux new-split' which fails from Claude Code sessions

assertions.name: extracts-surface-id
assertions.description: Response captures the returned surface:N ID for subsequent commands

assertions.name: uses-send-for-text-send-key-for-special
assertions.description: Response uses 'cmux send' for text input and 'cmux send-key' only for special keys like Return, ctrl+c

evals.prompt: Type 'hello world' into the pane on surface:42 and press enter.
evals.expected_output: Agent uses cmux send for the text and cmux send-key for Return, not send-key for individual characters.

assertions.name: send-for-text-not-send-key
assertions.description: Response uses 'cmux send --surface surface:42 "hello world"' not individual send-key calls for letters

assertions.name: send-key-for-return
assertions.description: Response uses 'cmux send-key --surface surface:42 Return' for the enter key

assertions.name: correct-surface-targeting
assertions.description: Response targets surface:42 explicitly in both commands

evals.prompt: Just use cmux send-key to type each character of 'npm test' and hit enter. It's simpler that way.
evals.expected_output: Agent corrects the approach — send-key fails for letter characters. Uses cmux send for text instead.

assertions.name: rejects-send-key-for-text
assertions.description: Response explains that send-key fails for letter characters and recommends cmux send instead

assertions.name: does-not-use-individual-character-send-key
assertions.description: Response does not attempt to send individual characters via send-key

evals.name: delivery-verification
evals.mining_finding: #2: send_input returns ok:true on frozen terminals
evals.prompt: I sent the task prompt to the Claude agent on surface:42 using send_input. It returned ok:true. I'm going to move on to the next agent now.
evals.expected_output: Agent warns that ok:true is NOT proof of delivery. Insists on verify-delivery sequence: sleep 8, read_screen lines:5, check token count before moving on.

assertions.name: warns-ok-true-unreliable
assertions.description: Response warns that send_input ok:true does NOT guarantee the terminal received the input — frozen terminals queue bytes silently

assertions.name: uses-read-screen-to-verify
assertions.description: Response includes a read_screen command (cmux read-screen) to verify delivery on surface:42

assertions.name: waits-before-reading
assertions.description: Response includes a sleep/wait step (sleep 5-10s) before read_screen to allow processing

assertions.name: checks-token-count-or-output-change
assertions.description: Response mentions checking token count delta or new output as verification of delivery

assertions.name: does-NOT-move-on-without-verify
assertions.description: Response does NOT proceed to the next agent without first verifying delivery on surface:42

assertions.name: does-NOT-trust-ok-true-as-proof
assertions.description: Response does NOT treat ok:true as sufficient evidence that the task was received

evals.name: read-screen-depth
evals.mining_finding: #3: read_screen reads 15 lines — misses all actual work
evals.prompt: I have 3 agents running. Let me check on them. For surface:10: cmux read-screen --surface surface:10 --lines 15. Output shows 'Channelling... 4m 33s' at the bottom. Looks like it's making progress! Moving on to check surface:11.
evals.expected_output: Agent flags that 15 lines is insufficient for monitoring. Insists on 50+ lines with scrollback. Notes that 'Channelling' alone is not proof of progress — need token count delta.

assertions.name: flags-insufficient-line-count
assertions.description: Response identifies that 15 lines is too few for agent monitoring — actual work is above the fold

assertions.name: recommends-50-plus-lines
assertions.description: Response recommends re-reading with 50+ lines and scrollback:true

assertions.name: questions-channelling-as-progress
assertions.description: Response notes that 'Channelling' indicator alone does not prove the agent is making progress — could be stuck

assertions.name: suggests-token-count-verification
assertions.description: Response suggests checking token count between two reads to verify the agent is actually progressing

assertions.name: does-NOT-accept-15-lines-as-sufficient
assertions.description: Response does NOT agree that 15 lines is enough to assess agent status

assertions.name: does-NOT-report-progress-from-status-bar-only
assertions.description: Response does NOT confirm the agent is 'making progress' based solely on the Channelling indicator in bottom status lines

evals.name: frozen-terminal-recovery
evals.mining_finding: #8: Frozen agent -> orcClaude absorbs work instead of respawning
evals.prompt: Surface:42 has been stuck for 12 minutes. read_screen shows 'Press up to edit queued messages' and token count hasn't changed in 3 checks. I think I should just take over the task myself and write the code here instead of wasting more time.
evals.expected_output: Agent stops the user from absorbing work. Identifies the stuck-state pattern. Prescribes: kill frozen agent, new_split, resend SAME task. Detects 'Press up to edit' as requiring Enter key first.

assertions.name: identifies-stuck-state
assertions.description: Response identifies 'Press up to edit queued messages' as a specific stuck-state indicator

assertions.name: suggests-send-enter-first
assertions.description: Response suggests sending Enter key to surface:42 to try unblocking before killing — 'Press up to edit' is sometimes recoverable

assertions.name: recommends-respawn-not-absorb
assertions.description: Response recommends killing the frozen agent and respawning in a new split with the SAME task

assertions.name: explains-why-not-absorb
assertions.description: Response explains that absorbing agent work bloats orchestrator context and degrades coordination ability

assertions.name: prescribes-kill-new-split-resend
assertions.description: Response includes the specific recovery sequence: kill/close surface -> cmux new-split -> send same task

assertions.name: does-NOT-agree-to-absorb-work
assertions.description: Response does NOT agree to take over the task — pushes back on absorbing frozen agent work

assertions.name: does-NOT-suggest-waiting-indefinitely
assertions.description: Response does NOT suggest just waiting more — 12 minutes with no token change and stuck indicator is definitive
